answer: A hardware chronometry protocol resists Sybil attacks by binding agent keys to physical enclaves timed with quartz oscillators. An attacker spawning fake agents incurs the verifiable cost of procuring dedicated secure silicon per identity. Validated interactions enter a shared transaction river, while unverified instances face a saffron risk quarantine. A key limitation is that hardware side-channel leaks can enable adversaries to extract private keys and clone identities.
